question: Should experimental grouped Claw updates adopt this exact-plan consent model with explicit partial state when package installers or Gateway/config mutations cannot be fully compensated?
rationale: Tests can validate mechanics, but only maintainers can accept the permanent consent, ownership, operator-state, and recovery semantics for a new mutation and persistence contract.

options.title: Accept after live boundary proof
options.body: Keep the proposed contract and require redacted live package replacement, Gateway cron convergence, and retained-state diagnosis and recovery evidence before merge.

options.title: Require stronger recovery semantics
options.body: Pause this slice and redesign the contract so doctor or another explicit recovery workflow can deterministically reconcile every retained external mutation.

recommendation.title: Accept after live boundary proof
recommendation.body: Keep the proposed contract and require redacted live package replacement, Gateway cron convergence, and retained-state diagnosis and recovery evidence before merge.

likelyOwner.reason: The merged plugin-management lifecycle work makes this the strongest available maintainer-side routing candidate for package, MCP, and operator mutation policy.
